Paragraph:
Translation: There are many other heroes who are prepared to lay down their lives for my sake. All of them are well equipped with different kinds of weapons, and all are experienced in military science.

Purport (Excerpt): As far as the others are concerned—like Jayadratha, Krtavarma, Salya, etc.—all are determined to lay down their lives for Duryodhana's sake. In other words, it is already concluded that all of them would die in the Battle of Kuruksetra for joining the party of the sinful Duryodhana. Duryodhana was, of course, confident of his victory on account of the above-mentioned combined strength of his friends.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Duryodhana continues to inventory his forces, boasting about the vast number of experienced heroes who are armed and willing to sacrifice their lives for him, thereby masking his earlier anxiety with inflated confidence.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: He broadens his focus from specific elite commanders to the sheer volume and dedication of his overall army. The commentary points out the grim irony: their readiness to die for him is a self-fulfilling prophecy, as aligning with his unrighteous cause guarantees their destruction.
Outcome/Resolution: Duryodhana successfully (but temporarily) deludes himself into a state of absolute confidence based solely on the material strength and professed loyalty of his allies.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.attachment: Codependency (seeking validation through the sacrifice of others)

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Moha (Deep illusion; mistaking material readiness for guaranteed success while ignoring moral reality)
Avidya (Ignorance; the inability to see that siding with adharma leads only to ruin)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The verse illustrates the pinnacle of material delusion. Duryodhana calculates his victory based on weapons, numbers, and the blind loyalty of his men, completely missing the spiritual reality that any force allied with adharma (unrighteousness) is already defeated by cosmic design.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Duryodhana demonstrates a severe cognitive distortion: delusional grandiosity. To suppress his underlying terror, he swings to the opposite extreme, constructing a false reality where the sheer volume of his supporters makes him invincible. This reflects a fragile ego protecting itself through absolute denial of the actual risk.
